     1	# Phase 4 R1 — Web demo page designs (Checkpoint 1)
     2	
     3	Three Crystal demo entries, each emitting one self-contained HTML file
     4	that wraps the `*WithWebFallback` web visitor output in a minimal page
     5	with one trigger element. The HTML files are written under
     6	`samples/cross_platform/web/dist/` at build time so the CDP harness can
     7	load them via `file://`.
     8	
     9	The three entries use the actual UI tree → `UI::Web::Renderer` →
    10	`render_to_html` pipeline, NOT a hand-crafted DOM. That keeps the test
    11	honest: if the visitor emission drifts, the demo drifts with it and
    12	the CDP probe catches the regression.
    13	
    14	## Shared scaffold (Crystal side)
    15	
    16	```crystal
    17	require "../../../src/ui/views"
    18	require "../../../src/ui/renderers/web_renderer"
    19	require "../../../src/ui/design_tokens"
    20	require "../../../src/ui/design_tokens/generators/web_generator"
    21	
    22	renderer = UI::Web::Renderer.new
    23	inner_html = renderer.render(root_view) # markup for the WithWebFallback subtree
    24	token_css = UI::DesignTokens::WebGenerator.generate(
    25	  UI::DesignTokens::Tokens.default,
    26	)
    27	
    28	html = <<-HTML
    29	<!doctype html><html lang="en"><head>
    30	  <meta charset="utf-8">
    31	  <meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width,initial-scale=1">
    32	  <title>...</title>
    33	  <style>#{token_css}</style>
    34	  <style>html,body{margin:0;font-family:var(--ap-font-sans);background:var(--ap-color-surface-canvas);color:var(--ap-color-text-primary)}</style>

    42	## Page 1 — `phase04_action_sheet_demo.cr` → `phase04_action_sheet_demo.html`
    43	
    44	Tree:
    45	
    46	```
    47	VStack [main]
    48	  Button "Open sheet" data-testid="action-sheet-trigger"
    49	  ActionSheetWithWebFallback (is_presented: true)
    50	    title: "Action sheet demo"
    51	    message: "Pick a destructive option."
    52	    add_action("Save",        :default)
    53	    add_action("Delete",      :destructive)
    54	    add_action("Cancel",      :cancel)
    55	```
    56	
    57	Why these choices:
    58	* `is_presented: true` so the sheet is in the DOM with
    59	  `data-presented="true"` at page load → CDP probes don't need to
    60	  click-open before measuring positioning / touch targets / axe / IBM.
    61	  Focus-trap and dismissal probes will toggle `data-presented` via
    62	  `__phase4Open()` helpers exposed on `window` (see helpers below).
    63	* One destructive + one default + one cancel action exercises the
    64	  three CSS variants and gives the touch-target probe 3 buttons +
    65	  the cancel button to measure.
    66	* The trigger button lives OUTSIDE the sheet so it is the natural
    67	  "previously focused" element for focus-restoration assertions.
    68	
    69	Exposed helpers (added in a `<script>` block AFTER the visitor's
    70	inlined fallback script so the fallback handlers exist first):
    71	
    72	```js
    73	window.__phase4 = {
    74	  trigger() { return document.querySelector('[data-testid="action-sheet-trigger"]'); },
    75	  sheet()   { return document.querySelector('.ap-action-sheet'); },
    76	  panel()   { return document.querySelector('.ap-action-sheet__panel'); },
    77	  backdrop(){ return document.querySelector('.ap-action-sheet__backdrop'); },
    78	  open() {
    79	    window.__phase4.trigger().focus();
    80	    window.__preOpenFocus = document.activeElement;
    81	    window.__phase4DismissLog = [];
    82	    window.__phase4.sheet().addEventListener('ap:action-sheet:dismiss',
    83	      e => window.__phase4DismissLog.push(e.detail));
    84	    window.__phase4.sheet().setAttribute('data-presented', 'true');
    85	  },
    86	  focusables() {
    87	    return Array.from(window.__phase4.panel().querySelectorAll(
    88	      'a[href],button:not([disabled]),input:not([disabled]),' +
    89	      'select:not([disabled]),textarea:not([disabled]),' +
    90	      '[tabindex]:not([tabindex="-1"])'
    91	    ));
    92	  }
    93	};
    94	```
    95	
    96	The `__phase4.open()` helper sets `data-presented='true'` which fires
    97	the fallback's MutationObserver and runs its `show()` bookkeeping
    98	(focus first focusable, stash previouslyFocused). This matches what
    99	a real "open" trigger would do in app code.

   101	## Page 2 — `phase04_context_menu_demo.cr` → `phase04_context_menu_demo.html`
   102	
   103	Tree:
   104	
   105	```
   106	VStack
   107	  Button "Top-left trigger"     data-testid="ctx-trigger-tl"      (positioned absolute top:0 left:0)
   108	  Button "Center trigger"       data-testid="ctx-trigger-center"  (centered)
   109	  Button "Bottom-right trigger" data-testid="ctx-trigger-br"      (positioned bottom:0 right:0)
   110	
   111	  -- three independent ContextMenuWithWebFallback instances, one per trigger --
   112	  ContextMenuWithWebFallback (trigger: btn-tl)
   113	    items: ["Open", "Rename", "Duplicate" (disabled), Separator, "Delete" (destructive)]
   114	  ContextMenuWithWebFallback (trigger: btn-center)
   115	    items: (same)
   116	  ContextMenuWithWebFallback (trigger: btn-br)
   117	    items: (same)
   118	```
   119	
   120	Why:
   121	* Three real triggers in three viewport quadrants satisfies
   122	  `conformance.context-menu-positioning`'s "three real trigger positions"
   123	  requirement.
   124	* One disabled item lets `focus.context-menu-keyboard-nav` verify
   125	  Arrow / Home / End skip it. Adding `data-test-disabled="true"`
   126	  via post-render JS is unnecessary because the visitor already
   127	  emits `aria-disabled="true"` and the validator can use that.
   128	* The destructive item exercises the `--destructive` CSS class.
   129	
   130	Wait — `ContextMenuWithWebFallback` is `View` (not container), so we
   131	can't add it as a child of `VStack` unless `VStack` accepts arbitrary
   132	`View`s. Confirm: VStack#<<(View) is the contract. It does. The
   133	trigger is passed via the `trigger:` property to the menu instance.
   134	
   135	The buttons are emitted twice in the DOM: once as standalone
   136	`VStack` children (so they have a positioning rail) and once as the
   137	host's first child (because the renderer renders `trigger.accept(self)`
   138	INSIDE the host wrapper). This double-render is a concern — see
   139	"Open question" below.
   140	
   141	**Resolution:** Don't put the buttons in the VStack at all. Only
   142	attach them as `trigger:` of each ContextMenuWithWebFallback. The
   143	host wrapper has `position: relative; display: contents;` so the
   144	trigger renders in normal flow. Positioning the host (or the trigger
   145	directly) via inline `style` attributes done by adding `add_style`
   146	on the trigger view solves the quadrant placement.
   147	
   148	Exposed helpers:
   149	
   150	```js
   151	window.__phase4 = {
   152	  triggers: {
   153	    tl:     document.querySelector('[data-testid="ctx-trigger-tl"]'),
   154	    center: document.querySelector('[data-testid="ctx-trigger-center"]'),
   155	    br:     document.querySelector('[data-testid="ctx-trigger-br"]'),
   156	  },
   157	  menus: () => Array.from(document.querySelectorAll('.ap-ctx-menu')),
   158	  menuFor(testid) {
   159	    var trigger = document.querySelector('[data-testid="' + testid + '"]');
   160	    var host = trigger.closest('[data-ap-ctx-host]');
   161	    return host.querySelector('.ap-ctx-menu');
   162	  },
   163	  dismissLog: [],
   164	};
   165	document.querySelectorAll('[data-ap-ctx-host]').forEach(host => {
   166	  host.addEventListener('ap:ctx-menu:dismiss',
   167	    e => window.__phase4.dismissLog.push({reason: e.detail.reason, host: host}));
   168	});
   169	```

   185	Why minimal: the only Phase 4 R1 work on this widget is the axe-core /

   187	already covered by `spec/ui/views/path_control_with_web_fallback_spec.cr`
   188	(passed in iter 1). No JS interaction probes needed.
   189	
   190	## Cross-cutting page concerns
   191	
   192	1. **Color scheme:** the harness will set
   193	   `Emulation.setEmulatedMedia({features: [{name: "prefers-color-scheme", value: "light"|"dark"}]})`
   194	   for the dual-scheme axe/IBM captures. The token CSS already
   195	   responds to `prefers-color-scheme`, so no in-page toggle needed.
   196	2. **Viewport:** harness drives via `Emulation.setDeviceMetricsOverride`.
   197	   The action sheet probe captures at 1280x800 (desktop), 375x667
   198	   (mobile), 320x568 (mobile-min).
   199	3. **Safe-area insets:** headless Chrome defaults `safe-area-inset-bottom`
   200	   to 0, so the bottom-position predicate `rect.bottom === innerHeight`
   201	   holds.
   202	4. **Inline CSS reset:** body margin reset is the only global style
   203	   added to make rect math deterministic.
   204	
   205	## Open questions for Codex
   206	
   207	1. The context-menu page renders THREE `ContextMenuWithWebFallback`
   208	   instances on one page. The renderer only emits the
   209	   CSS/script blocks the FIRST time it visits this class (per
   210	   `@context_menu_css_emitted` guard). Verify this works for three
   211	   instances: the CSS/script lives in the first host only, but the
   212	   fallback JS's `init()` queries `[data-ap-ctx-host]` document-wide
   213	   and attaches to all three. Should be fine.
   214	
   215	2. The action-sheet renderer's `@action_sheet_css_emitted` guard
   216	   means we only get the JS once. We have only one sheet per page,
   217	   so non-issue.
   218	
   219	3. The fallback JS uses `MutationObserver` on `document.documentElement`
   220	   to re-init when new sheets / menus are inserted. This means
   221	   `init()` runs on every DOM mutation. Acceptable cost for a test
   222	   page; not a probe concern.
   223	
   224	4. The `__phase4.open()` helper for action-sheet sets
   225	   `data-presented='true'`. The fallback's MutationObserver picks
   226	   that up and runs `show()`, which calls `requestAnimationFrame`
   227	   before focusing. The CDP probe must poll until `document.activeElement`
   228	   is inside the panel before declaring "open complete". Easy.
   229	
   230	5. **IBM Equal Access on a page that loads sentinel JS**: the IBM
   231	   audit injects its own script. The fallback scripts and our
   232	   `__phase4` script should NOT trigger IBM violations themselves
   233	   (no inline event handlers, no missing alt attrs in the bridge
   234	   code). Verify with a smoke run after assembly.
   235	
   236	6. Should we audit axe/IBM AFTER the sheet is opened (presented)?
   237	   Yes — the rubric explicitly says "presented" and the more
   238	   interesting accessibility surface is the live dialog tree.

     1	// Vanilla-JS bottom-sheet behavior for UI::ActionSheetWithWebFallback.
     2	// Pure DOM; no framework. Idempotent — safe to register multiple times
     3	// (guarded by window.__apActionSheetInitialized).
     4	//
     5	// Behaviors:
     6	//   * Backdrop click dismisses (treated as 'backdrop')
     7	//   * Escape key dismisses (treated as 'escape')
     8	//   * Focus trap inside the panel while presented
     9	//   * On show: save previously focused element, focus first action
    10	//   * On dismiss: restore focus to previously focused element
    11	//   * Optional swipe-down on the handle dismisses on touch devices
    12	//
    13	// Custom-event contract with Crystal-side hosts:
    14	//   * Crystal emits <div class="ap-action-sheet" data-presented="true|false">.
    15	//   * Toggling data-presented opens/closes the sheet.
    16	//   * Action clicks dispatch CustomEvent("ap:action-sheet:action",
    17	//     { detail: { index, label } }) on the root element.
    18	//   * Any dismissal dispatches CustomEvent("ap:action-sheet:dismiss",
    19	//     { detail: { reason } }).
    20	(function () {
    21	  if (window.__apActionSheetInitialized) return;
    22	  window.__apActionSheetInitialized = true;
    23	
    24	  var FOCUSABLE =
    25	    'a[href],button:not([disabled]),input:not([disabled]),' +
    26	    'select:not([disabled]),textarea:not([disabled]),[tabindex]:not([tabindex="-1"])';
    27	
    28	  var state = new WeakMap();
    29	
    30	  function focusables(panel) {
    31	    return Array.prototype.filter.call(
    32	      panel.querySelectorAll(FOCUSABLE),
    33	      function (el) { return el.offsetParent !== null || el === document.activeElement; }
    34	    );
    35	  }
    36	
    37	  function trapFocus(e, root) {
    38	    if (e.key !== 'Tab') return;
    39	    var panel = root.querySelector('.ap-action-sheet__panel');
    40	    if (!panel) return;
    41	    var els = focusables(panel);
    42	    if (els.length === 0) { e.preventDefault(); panel.focus(); return; }
    43	    var first = els[0], last = els[els.length - 1];
    44	    if (e.shiftKey && document.activeElement === first) {
    45	      e.preventDefault(); last.focus();
    46	    } else if (!e.shiftKey && document.activeElement === last) {
    47	      e.preventDefault(); first.focus();
    48	    }
    49	  }
    50	
    51	  function show(root) {
    52	    var s = state.get(root) || {};
    53	    s.previouslyFocused = document.activeElement;
    54	    state.set(root, s);
    55	    var panel = root.querySelector('.ap-action-sheet__panel');
    56	    if (!panel) return;
    57	    var first = focusables(panel)[0] || panel;
    58	    requestAnimationFrame(function () { first.focus(); });
    59	  }
    60	
    61	  function hide(root, reason) {
    62	    var s = state.get(root);
    63	    root.setAttribute('data-presented', 'false');
    64	    root.dispatchEvent(new CustomEvent('ap:action-sheet:dismiss',
    65	      { detail: { reason: reason } }));
    66	    if (s && s.previouslyFocused && typeof s.previouslyFocused.focus === 'function') {
    67	      s.previouslyFocused.focus();
    68	    }
    69	  }
    70	
    71	  function attach(root) {
    72	    if (root.__apBound) return;
    73	    root.__apBound = true;
    74	
    75	    root.addEventListener('click', function (e) {
    76	      var dismiss = e.target.closest('[data-ap-as-dismiss]');
    77	      if (dismiss) {
    78	        e.preventDefault();
    79	        hide(root, dismiss.getAttribute('data-ap-as-dismiss'));
    80	        return;
    81	      }
    82	      var action = e.target.closest('[data-ap-as-action]');
    83	      if (action) {
    84	        e.preventDefault();
    85	        var index = parseInt(action.getAttribute('data-ap-as-action'), 10);
    86	        root.dispatchEvent(new CustomEvent('ap:action-sheet:action', {
    87	          detail: { index: index, label: (action.textContent || '').trim() }
    88	        }));
    89	        hide(root, 'action');
    90	      }
    91	    });
    92	
    93	    root.addEventListener('keydown', function (e) {
    94	      if (e.key === 'Escape') { e.preventDefault(); hide(root, 'escape'); return; }
    95	      trapFocus(e, root);
    96	    });
    97	
    98	    var handle = root.querySelector('.ap-action-sheet__handle');
    99	    if (handle && 'ontouchstart' in window) {
   100	      var startY = null;
   101	      handle.addEventListener('touchstart', function (e) {
   102	        startY = e.touches[0].clientY;
   103	      }, { passive: true });
   104	      handle.addEventListener('touchmove', function (e) {
   105	        if (startY === null) return;
   106	        var dy = e.touches[0].clientY - startY;
   107	        if (dy > 48) { hide(root, 'swipe'); startY = null; }
   108	      }, { passive: true });
   109	    }
   110	
   111	    // Watch the root for data-presented flips so show() bookkeeping runs.
   112	    // Scope: this single root only. attributeFilter narrows to the one
   113	    // attribute the JS cares about.
   114	    new MutationObserver(function (records) {
   115	      for (var i = 0; i < records.length; i++) {
   116	        var r = records[i];
   117	        if (r.attributeName === 'data-presented' &&
   118	            root.getAttribute('data-presented') === 'true') {
   119	          show(root);
   120	        }
   121	      }
   122	    }).observe(root, { attributes: true, attributeFilter: ['data-presented'] });
   123	
   124	    if (root.getAttribute('data-presented') === 'true') show(root);
   125	  }
   126	
   127	  function init() {
   128	    var roots = document.querySelectorAll('.ap-action-sheet');
   129	    for (var i = 0; i < roots.length; i++) attach(roots[i]);
   130	  }
   131	
   132	  if (document.readyState !== 'loading') init();
   133	  else document.addEventListener('DOMContentLoaded', init);
   134	
   135	  // Re-bind when new sheets are inserted by Crystal re-renders. Scope
   136	  // is document-wide because new roots could be inserted anywhere in
   137	  // the layout; childList only minimizes work.
   138	  new MutationObserver(init).observe(document.documentElement,
   139	    { childList: true, subtree: true });
   140	})();

     1	// Vanilla-JS context-menu behavior for UI::ContextMenuWithWebFallback.
     2	// Pure DOM; no framework. Idempotent — safe to register multiple times
     3	// (guarded by window.__apContextMenuInitialized).
     4	//
     5	// Behaviors:
     6	//   * Trigger element opens menu on contextmenu (right-click) and long-press
     7	//   * Menu positions itself near the trigger, flips when near viewport edge
     8	//   * Arrow keys move focus between menuitems
     9	//   * Home/End jump to first/last
    10	//   * Escape closes; focus returns to trigger
    11	//   * Click outside dismisses
    12	//   * Enter/Space activates the focused item
    13	//   * Disabled items are skipped by keyboard nav and not clickable
    14	//
    15	// Custom-event contract with Crystal-side hosts:
    16	//   * Crystal emits <div class="ap-ctx-menu-host" data-ap-ctx-host>
    17	//     wrapping a trigger element + a <ul class="ap-ctx-menu">.
    18	//   * Action clicks dispatch CustomEvent("ap:ctx-menu:action",
    19	//     { detail: { index, label } }) on the host.
    20	//   * Any dismissal dispatches CustomEvent("ap:ctx-menu:dismiss",
    21	//     { detail: { reason } }).
    22	(function () {
    23	  if (window.__apContextMenuInitialized) return;
    24	  window.__apContextMenuInitialized = true;
    25	
    26	  function itemsOf(menu) {
    27	    return Array.prototype.filter.call(
    28	      menu.querySelectorAll('.ap-ctx-menu__item'),
    29	      function (el) { return el.getAttribute('aria-disabled') !== 'true'; }
    30	    );
    31	  }
    32	
    33	  function position(menu, x, y) {
    34	    menu.setAttribute('data-presented', 'true');
    35	    var r = menu.getBoundingClientRect();
    36	    var vw = window.innerWidth, vh = window.innerHeight;
    37	    var left = (x + r.width > vw) ? Math.max(0, vw - r.width - 8) : x;
    38	    var top  = (y + r.height > vh) ? Math.max(0, vh - r.height - 8) : y;
    39	    menu.style.left = left + 'px';
    40	    menu.style.top  = top  + 'px';
    41	  }
    42	
    43	  function open(host, x, y) {
    44	    var menu = host.querySelector('.ap-ctx-menu');
    45	    if (!menu) return;
    46	    host.__previouslyFocused = document.activeElement;
    47	    position(menu, x, y);
    48	    var first = itemsOf(menu)[0];
    49	    if (first) first.focus();
    50	  }
    51	
    52	  function close(host, reason) {
    53	    var menu = host.querySelector('.ap-ctx-menu');
    54	    if (!menu) return;
    55	    menu.setAttribute('data-presented', 'false');
    56	    host.dispatchEvent(new CustomEvent('ap:ctx-menu:dismiss',
    57	      { detail: { reason: reason } }));
    58	    if (host.__previouslyFocused &&
    59	        typeof host.__previouslyFocused.focus === 'function') {
    60	      host.__previouslyFocused.focus();
    61	    }
    62	  }
    63	
    64	  function moveFocus(menu, dir) {
    65	    var items = itemsOf(menu);
    66	    if (items.length === 0) return;
    67	    var i = items.indexOf(document.activeElement);
    68	    var next;
    69	    if (dir === 'first')     next = 0;
    70	    else if (dir === 'last') next = items.length - 1;
    71	    else if (dir === 'next') next = i < 0 ? 0 : (i + 1) % items.length;
    72	    else if (dir === 'prev') next = i < 0 ? items.length - 1 : (i - 1 + items.length) % items.length;
    73	    items[next].focus();
    74	  }
    75	
    76	  // Skip elements that can never be triggers (per-host inline <style>,
    77	  // <script>, and the menu itself).
    78	  function isTriggerCandidate(el) {
    79	    if (el.classList.contains('ap-ctx-menu')) return false;
    80	    var tag = el.tagName;
    81	    if (tag === 'STYLE' || tag === 'SCRIPT' || tag === 'TEMPLATE') return false;
    82	    return true;
    83	  }
    84	
    85	  function findTrigger(host) {
    86	    var children = Array.prototype.slice.call(host.children);
    87	    for (var i = 0; i < children.length; i++) {
    88	      if (isTriggerCandidate(children[i])) return children[i];
    89	    }
    90	    return null;
    91	  }
    92	
    93	  // Tab/Shift+Tab focus trap inside an open menu.
    94	  function trapFocus(e, menu) {
    95	    if (e.key !== 'Tab') return;
    96	    var items = itemsOf(menu);
    97	    if (items.length === 0) { e.preventDefault(); return; }
    98	    var first = items[0], last = items[items.length - 1];
    99	    if (e.shiftKey && document.activeElement === first) {
   100	      e.preventDefault(); last.focus();
   101	    } else if (!e.shiftKey && document.activeElement === last) {
   102	      e.preventDefault(); first.focus();
   103	    }
   104	  }
   105	
   106	  function attach(host) {
   107	    if (host.__apBound) return;
   108	    host.__apBound = true;
   109	
   110	    var trigger = findTrigger(host);
   111	    if (!trigger) return;
   112	
   113	    trigger.addEventListener('contextmenu', function (e) {
   114	      e.preventDefault();
   115	      open(host, e.clientX, e.clientY);
   116	    });
   117	
   118	    // Keyboard open path: Shift+F10 + the dedicated ContextMenu key
   119	    // (both common assistive-tech contracts). Browsers usually synthesize
   120	    // a `contextmenu` event for these, but binding explicitly is safer
   121	    // — especially when the trigger is not focused at the moment of the
   122	    // press. Open at the trigger's center so the menu lands somewhere
   123	    // sensible.
   124	    trigger.addEventListener('keydown', function (e) {
   125	      var isShiftF10 = e.shiftKey && e.key === 'F10';
   126	      var isContextKey = e.key === 'ContextMenu';
   127	      if (!isShiftF10 && !isContextKey) return;
   128	      e.preventDefault();
   129	      var r = trigger.getBoundingClientRect();
   130	      open(host, r.left + r.width / 2, r.top + r.height / 2);
   131	    });
   132	
   133	    var pressTimer = null;
   134	    trigger.addEventListener('touchstart', function (e) {
   135	      if (e.touches.length !== 1) return;
   136	      var t = e.touches[0];
   137	      pressTimer = setTimeout(function () { open(host, t.clientX, t.clientY); }, 500);
   138	    }, { passive: true });
   139	    ['touchend', 'touchmove', 'touchcancel'].forEach(function (ev) {
   140	      trigger.addEventListener(ev, function () { clearTimeout(pressTimer); }, { passive: true });
   141	    });
   142	
   143	    var menu = host.querySelector('.ap-ctx-menu');
   144	    if (!menu) return;
   145	
   146	    menu.addEventListener('click', function (e) {
   147	      var item = e.target.closest('.ap-ctx-menu__item');
   148	      if (!item || item.getAttribute('aria-disabled') === 'true') return;
   149	      var index = parseInt(item.getAttribute('data-ap-ctx-action'), 10);
   150	      host.dispatchEvent(new CustomEvent('ap:ctx-menu:action', {
   151	        detail: { index: index, label: (item.textContent || '').trim() }
   152	      }));
   153	      close(host, 'action');
   154	    });
   155	
   156	    menu.addEventListener('keydown', function (e) {
   157	      switch (e.key) {
   158	        case 'Escape':    e.preventDefault(); close(host, 'escape'); break;
   159	        case 'ArrowDown': e.preventDefault(); moveFocus(menu, 'next'); break;
   160	        case 'ArrowUp':   e.preventDefault(); moveFocus(menu, 'prev'); break;
   161	        case 'Home':      e.preventDefault(); moveFocus(menu, 'first'); break;
   162	        case 'End':       e.preventDefault(); moveFocus(menu, 'last');  break;
   163	        case 'Tab':       trapFocus(e, menu); break;
   164	        case 'Enter':
   165	        case ' ':         e.preventDefault();
   166	          if (document.activeElement) document.activeElement.click();
   167	          break;
   168	      }
   169	    });
   170	
   171	    document.addEventListener('click', function (e) {
   172	      if (menu.getAttribute('data-presented') !== 'true') return;
   173	      if (host.contains(e.target)) return;
   174	      close(host, 'outside');
   175	    });
   176	  }
   177	
   178	  function init() {
   179	    var hosts = document.querySelectorAll('[data-ap-ctx-host]');
   180	    for (var i = 0; i < hosts.length; i++) attach(hosts[i]);
   181	  }
   182	
   183	  if (document.readyState !== 'loading') init();
   184	  else document.addEventListener('DOMContentLoaded', init);
   185	
   186	  new MutationObserver(init).observe(document.documentElement,
   187	    { childList: true, subtree: true });
   188	})();

docs/initiative-cross-platform-ui/rubric/behavior-simulation-toolkit.md:575:## 3. Web — Chrome DevTools Protocol (CDP) over WebSocket from Crystal
docs/initiative-cross-platform-ui/rubric/behavior-simulation-toolkit.md:579:The validator drives Chrome **directly** via the Chrome DevTools Protocol (CDP). No browser MCP, no Puppeteer, no Playwright. The canonical implementation is `scripts/capture_amber_demo_screenshots.cr`; new validator scripts must extend or copy that pattern, not reinvent it.
docs/initiative-cross-platform-ui/rubric/behavior-simulation-toolkit.md:581:The pattern in three sentences: spawn a headless Chrome with `--remote-debugging-port=<port>`; poll `http://127.0.0.1:<port>/json/version` until ready; open a `HTTP::WebSocket` to a new target's `webSocketDebuggerUrl` and exchange JSON-RPC messages (`{"id": N, "method": "...", "params": {...}}`). Every probe in this section reduces to a `Runtime.evaluate`, `Input.dispatchKeyEvent`, `Input.dispatchMouseEvent`, `Emulation.setDeviceMetricsOverride`, or `Page.captureScreenshot` call.
docs/initiative-cross-platform-ui/rubric/behavior-simulation-toolkit.md:583:The CDP surface relevant to behavior probing:
docs/initiative-cross-platform-ui/rubric/behavior-simulation-toolkit.md:585:| CDP method | Use |
docs/initiative-cross-platform-ui/rubric/behavior-simulation-toolkit.md:587:| `Page.navigate` | Load a URL (incl. `file://` for built demos) |
docs/initiative-cross-platform-ui/rubric/behavior-simulation-toolkit.md:591:| `Runtime.evaluate` | Evaluate JS in the page; supports `awaitPromise`, `returnByValue` |
docs/initiative-cross-platform-ui/rubric/behavior-simulation-toolkit.md:599:Most behavior probes are `Runtime.evaluate` because JS is the most expressive way to introspect rendered state. Trusted key/mouse synthesis goes through `Input.dispatchKeyEvent` / `Input.dispatchMouseEvent` — CDP input events are trusted by the browser, which is the entire reason this protocol is used for the keyboard-trust-gated focus probes (focus-trap libraries that gate on `event.isTrusted` respond to CDP input but reject JS-dispatched `KeyboardEvent`).

docs/initiative-cross-platform-ui/rubric/validation_criteria.md:33:**Behavior check.** "The element does the thing it claims to do, end to end." For a button: tap on the rendered surface (XCUITest tap, CDP `Input.dispatchMouseEvent` click or `Runtime.evaluate` `.click()` on web, AppKit synthetic event) fires the bound action handler, the bound state mutates, the next render reflects the new state, and any visible feedback (press animation, focus ring, haptic) plays. For a navigation: trigger the link, the next view becomes visible, the back affordance restores the previous view. For a modal: trigger open, the modal is in the accessibility tree; trigger each documented dismiss path (primary action, cancel, backdrop, escape key on web, swipe-down on iOS); confirm the modal is removed from the accessibility tree and focus returns to the trigger. Behavior is required for every Tier 2 and Tier 3 widget claim, every phase that wires a Crystal-side declaration to a native or web runtime, and every navigation flow.
docs/initiative-cross-platform-ui/rubric/validation_criteria.md:97:2. **Run the check.** Use the tools available (Bash for tests/builds/scripts, Read for file inspection, the CDP-via-Crystal harness in `scripts/capture_amber_demo_screenshots.cr` and its siblings for visual verification if relevant — see `rubric/behavior-simulation-toolkit.md` §3).

The actual API surface for each (which actions are wired today, which Carbon constants to invoke for unwired actions, how to assert focus restoration, how to drive a Tab cycle through a focus-trap, how to sample rendered geometry per platform) is documented in `rubric/behavior-simulation-toolkit.md`.      1	require "../platform_visitor"
     2	require "../../components"
     3	require "../design_tokens"
     4	require "../design_tokens/generators/web_generator"
     5	
     6	module UI
     7	  module Web
     8	    # Renders a UI view tree to HTML using the Components::Elements system.
     9	    #
    10	    # The renderer walks the view tree via the visitor pattern and produces
    11	    # an equivalent DOM tree built from `Components::Elements` classes.
    12	    # Call `render` on a view to get the final HTML string.
    13	    #
    14	    # Example:
    15	    #   label = UI::Label.new("Hello")
    16	    #   renderer = UI::Web::Renderer.new
    17	    #   label.accept(renderer)
    18	    #   renderer.output # => "<span style=\"font-size: 17.0px; color: rgba(0, 0, 0, 1.0); text-align: left\">Hello</span>"
    19	    class Renderer < UI::PlatformVisitor
    20	      # Stack of elements being built. The top of the stack is the current
    21	      # parent container that child elements will be added to.
    22	      @element_stack : Array(Components::Elements::HTMLElement)
    23	
    24	      # The root element produced by the most recent `visit` call at the
    25	      # top level.
    26	      @root : Components::Elements::HTMLElement?
    27	
    28	      property theme : UI::Theme? = nil
    29	
    30	      def initialize
    31	        @element_stack = [] of Components::Elements::HTMLElement
    32	        @root = nil
    33	      end
    34	
    35	      # The unified UI::DesignTokens model. Defaults to Tokens.default; can be
    36	      # swapped (with a brand override applied) by the host app before render.
    37	      property design_tokens : UI::DesignTokens::Tokens = UI::DesignTokens::Tokens.default
    38	
    39	      # Inject CSS custom properties from the active design tokens model as a
    40	      # <style> element at the beginning of the output.
    41	      #
    42	      # Phase 1 of the cross-platform UI initiative: this delegates entirely
    43	      # to UI::DesignTokens::WebGenerator so the renderer and the committed
    44	      # dist file share a single source of truth. The legacy UI::Theme
    45	      # custom-property block is emitted too for backward compatibility with
    46	      # callers that depend on `--md-sys-color-*` aliases.
    47	      def inject_theme_css : String
    48	        t = @theme || UI::Theme.design_system_default
    49	
    50	        String.build do |io|
    51	          io << "<style>\n"
    52	          io << t.to_css_custom_properties
    53	          io << UI::DesignTokens::WebGenerator.generate(@design_tokens)
    54	          io << "</style>\n"
    55	        end
    56	      end
    57	
    58	      # Returns the rendered HTML string for the view tree.
    59	      def output : String
    60	        @root.try(&.render) || ""
    61	      end
    62	
    63	      # Convenience method: accept a view and return the HTML string.
    64	      def render(view : UI::View) : String
    65	        view.accept(self)
    66	        output
    67	      end
    68	
    69	      # Render `view` wrapped in a full HTML5 document. Always emits the
    70	      # responsive viewport meta tag, the charset, the supplied title, and
    71	      # the active design-token `<style>` block (via `inject_theme_css`)
    72	      # before the rendered view in `<body>`. Callers therefore never need
    73	      # to hand-roll a `<head>` or remember the viewport meta — the
    74	      # renderer owns that responsibility for any consumer.
    75	      #
    76	      # `lang` defaults to `"en"` and can be overridden for localized output.
    77	      def render_document(view : UI::View, title : String, lang : String = "en") : String
    78	        body_html = render(view)
    79	        String.build do |str|
    80	          str << "<!doctype html>\n"
    81	          str << %(<html lang="#{lang}">) << '\n'
    82	          str << "<head>\n"
    83	          str << %(<meta charset="utf-8">) << '\n'
    84	          str << %(<meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1">) << '\n'
    85	          str << "<title>" << title << "</title>\n"
    86	          str << inject_theme_css
    87	          str << "</head>\n"
    88	          str << "<body>\n"
    89	          str << body_html
    90	          str << "\n</body>\n"
    91	          str << "</html>\n"
    92	        end
    93	      end
    94	
    95	      # ---------------------------------------------------------------
    96	      # Visit methods

Short answer: mostly yes, with two fixes before I’d trust the CDP probes.

1. `data-presented='true'` in `__phase4.open()`: yes, **if it changes from false to true**. The fallback watches that attribute and calls `show()`, which stores `document.activeElement` and focuses the first focusable on `requestAnimationFrame` in [action_sheet_fallback.js](/Users/crimsonknight/open_source_coding_projects/asset_pipeline/src/ui/web/action_sheet_fallback.js:51) and [action_sheet_fallback.js](/Users/crimsonknight/open_source_coding_projects/asset_pipeline/src/ui/web/action_sheet_fallback.js:114). But your page starts with `is_presented: true`, so the initial `show()` will stash body/current focus, not the trigger. For focus-restoration probes, make `open()` force a real transition:

```js
open() {
  const sheet = window.__phase4.sheet();
  window.__phase4.trigger().focus();
  window.__preOpenFocus = document.activeElement;
  window.__phase4DismissLog = [];
  sheet.setAttribute('data-presented', 'false');
  requestAnimationFrame(() => sheet.setAttribute('data-presented', 'true'));
}
```

Also attach the dismiss listener once, not inside every `open()`, or repeated probes will duplicate log entries.

2. Trigger-only context menus: yes. `VStack#<<` accepts any `View`, and the web renderer renders the `trigger` before the menu inside each host in [web_renderer.cr](/Users/crimsonknight/open_source_coding_projects/asset_pipeline/src/ui/renderers/web_renderer.cr:1549). `findTrigger()` will pick that direct child correctly in [context_menu_fallback.js](/Users/crimsonknight/open_source_coding_projects/asset_pipeline/src/ui/web/context_menu_fallback.js:85). I also rendered a three-menu tree locally and confirmed it emits 3 hosts, 3 trigger test IDs, and 3 menus.

One caveat: `UI::Button` does not expose a generic `add_style`; positioning via “add_style on the trigger view” is not available from the UI view API. Use page-level CSS targeting `[data-testid="ctx-trigger-*"]`, or add a deliberate view-level styling hook.

3. Three context menus on one page: fine with one renderer. The guard emits CSS/JS only for the first instance in [web_renderer.cr](/Users/crimsonknight/open_source_coding_projects/asset_pipeline/src/ui/renderers/web_renderer.cr:1605), and the script’s `init()` queries all `[data-ap-ctx-host]` document-wide in [context_menu_fallback.js](/Users/crimsonknight/open_source_coding_projects/asset_pipeline/src/ui/web/context_menu_fallback.js:178). Since inline script runs while the document is loading, it waits for `DOMContentLoaded`, so later hosts in the same HTML file are present before binding.

Axe/focus/escape should have what they need: action sheet has dialog labelling and focusable actions; context menu opens, focuses the first enabled item, skips disabled items, traps Tab, and Escape restores focus. Just make the action-sheet behavior probe reopen from a closed state and wait for focus to enter the panel before assertions.
